      - region "Simple English explanation of Tangent Plane":
        - paragraph: In simple English
        - heading "Understand Tangent Plane" [level=2]
        - paragraph: "A tangent plane is the flat plane that best matches a surface near a point. A useful rule is Tangent plane: z-z0=f_x(x0,y0)(x-x0)+f_y(x0,y0)(y-y0). You can learn Tangent Plane by trying one small example instead of long theory."
        - paragraph: "Use Tangent plane: z-z0=f_x(x0,y0)(x-x0)+f_y(x0,y0)(y-y0). Try the example below. Write your steps and choose an answer before opening the comparison."
        - paragraph: "In real life, engineering design: 3D formulas check shape, strength, and capacity. Watch out: Thinking the tangent plane matches the whole surface. It is a local approximation."
        - complementary:
          - generic: Try this example
          - paragraph: A tangent plane is mainly local or global?
          - generic "Compare your answer"
      - region "Tangent plane":
        - text: 3D MATHEMATICS 3D FUNCTIONS AND SURFACES
        - heading "Tangent Plane" [level=1]
        - paragraph: Approximate surfaces locally.
        - generic: ♧ Level
        - text: Advanced
        - generic: ▣ Topic

        - generic: Class
        - text: Class 12+

        - text: 6-10 min

        - complementary: "⊙ Objective: Approximate a surface near a point using its tangent plane."
        - navigation:

        - text: INTERACT
        - heading "Explore the surface, tangent plane & local approximation" [level=2]
        - article:
          - text: Surface

          - generic: ♧ Drag the blue point on the surface to move (a,b).
          - button "↻ Reset view"
        - complementary:
          - heading "1. Choose point (a,b)" [level=3]
          - text: a (x)
          - slider "a coordinate": "0.598407346410207"
          - status: "0.60"
          - text: b (y)
          - slider "b coordinate": "0.298407346410207"
          - status: "0.30"
          - heading "2. Live partial derivatives" [level=3]
          - text: f(a,b)
          - generic: "0.5394"
          - text: fₓ(a,b)
          - generic: "0.7885"
          - text: fᵧ(a,b)
          - generic: "-0.1669"
          - heading "3. Tangent plane (z=T)" [level=3]
          - status:
            - text: z=0.5394+0.7885(x-0.6)
            - text: −0.1669(y-0.3)
          - heading "4. Local approximation error" [level=3]

          - text: "0.1094"
          - strong: ✓ Small error near P — good fit!
        - article:
          - heading "At the point P(a,b,f(a,b))" [level=3]
          - paragraph: a=0.6, b=0.3
          - paragraph: f(a,b)=sin(0.6)cos(0.3)=0.5394
          - paragraph: fₓ(a,b)=cos(a)cos(b)=0.7885
          - paragraph: fᵧ(a,b)=-sin(a)sin(b)=-0.1669
        - article:
          - heading "Why this plane?" [level=3]
          - paragraph: The tangent plane matches the surface value and slope in both x and y directions at P.
          - paragraph: ✓ Same height at P
          - paragraph: ✓ Same slope in x-direction
          - paragraph: ✓ Same slope in y-direction
          - paragraph: ✓ Best linear approximation nearby
        - article:

          - paragraph: Zoom in near P (use smaller view window) to see the plane hugging the surface.
          - button "⌕ Zoom to neighborhood"
        - text: WORKED EXAMPLE
        - 'heading "Example: Find the tangent plane to f(x,y)=x²y+sin y at (1,π/6)" [level=2]'
        - article:
          - generic: "1"
          - heading "Compute values" [level=3]
          - paragraph: f(1,π/6)=1²(π/6)+sin(π/6)=π/6+1/2
        - article:
          - generic: "2"
          - heading "Partial derivatives" [level=3]
          - paragraph: fₓ=2xy ⇒ fₓ(1,π/6)=π/3
          - paragraph: fᵧ=x²+cos y ⇒ fᵧ(1,π/6)=1+√3/2
        - article:
          - generic: "3"
          - heading "Tangent plane" [level=3]
          - paragraph: z=f(a,b)+fₓ(a,b)(x-a)+fᵧ(a,b)(y-b)
        - strong: "Check: Substitute (x,y)=(1,π/6); both surface and plane give z=π/6+1/2."
        - article:
          - heading "KEY RULE (DEFINITION)" [level=3]
          - heading "Tangent Plane to z=f(x,y) at (a,b)" [level=2]
          - paragraph: If f has continuous first partial derivatives near (a,b), then the tangent plane at P(a,b,f(a,b)) is
          - status: z=f(a,b)+fₓ(a,b)(x-a)+fᵧ(a,b)(y-b)
          - paragraph: where fₓ and fᵧ are the partial derivatives.
        - article:
          - heading "MISCONCEPTION ALERT" [level=3]
          - paragraph: "Common mistake: Using (x,y) instead of (x-a,y-b)."
          - paragraph: The shifts (x-a) and (y-b) are essential for the plane to pass through P.
